limitations: Finite-input equivalence to existing student arithmetic, not native quality.

Exact full-image results cover only the checked checkpoints, inputs and environment.
Intervals average ten consecutive graph replays; p95 is an interval-average percentile, not per-frame tail latency.
Measured execution of experimental students plus grade, excluding D3D12 integration. No native-runtime acceleration.
One static input and one device; other desktop GPU work is not controlled.

native_chain_selftest.scope: Original integer kernels on fresh private buffers. No native model kernels are changed; finite tests cannot establish universal NVAPI ordering guarantees.

limitations: The straight-through gradient is intentionally a surrogate. Exact forward output does not imply an exact clamp derivative.
The training change improves eight validation frames and regresses eight. No quality acceptance or model installation.
These sixteen static validation frames stay outside training, but are repeatedly consulted during research; they are not a final independent test set.
Clipping accounts for only about eight percent of error on brighter training images and is not established as the main quality bottleneck.
Student graph timings include full-1080p network and output grade, exclude D3D12 integration, and average ten replays per interval.
The native selftest uses only original integer kernels, fresh buffers and a separate queue, on one GPU/driver. It is not a universal API ordering guarantee.
Native packed-argument lifetimes, complete command coverage, barriers and output/timing equivalence remain prerequisites for any real-model batching.
No native model kernel is modified or accelerated. One hidden sample launch, zero game launches, normal runtime files restored.
